title: Why the two SDs differ
statement:
```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([5, 6, 6, 12])
print(np.std(s), s.std())
```

The two printed numbers are different. Why?

[_]{a}

choices: pandas uses the median instead of the mean
`np.std` divides by N; pandas' `.std()` divides by N − 1
explanations: Both measure deviations from the mean.
Every value is used by both.
Correct: pandas reports the sample SD.

hints: Both use the same deviations from the mean.
solution: NumPy uses N (population SD); pandas uses N − 1 (sample SD), so pandas' value is slightly larger: 2.773 vs 3.202.
